findings.evidence: KeePass must be downloaded and installed
findings.rationale: Passive voice omits which actor (e.g., user or administrator) performs the download and installation, as well as the download source and target platform.

findings.evidence: Folder selected must be of type the database can read and that is “name”.kdb
findings.rationale: The pronoun 'that' has two plausible antecedents ('Folder selected' vs. 'type'), and referring to a '.kdb' file as a 'Folder' creates an unclear entity reference.

findings.evidence: Folder selected must be of type the database can read and that is “name”.kdb
findings.rationale: Specifies a file-type validation constraint without stating who selects the item or what happens if an unreadable or non-'.kdb' item is selected.

findings.evidence: Databases must have different names or else the previews one will be replace if selected
findings.rationale: 'if selected' and 'the previews one' have unclear attachment and reference (unclear whether selection refers to opening, creating, or saving a database, and whether name uniqueness is scoped to a folder or global).

findings.evidence: will be replace if selected
findings.rationale: Omits the operation and scope in which duplicate database names cause replacement, the actor performing the selection, and whether user confirmation or a warning is required before overwriting.

findings.evidence: There must be entries in the database in order for them to be printed
findings.rationale: Passive voice ('to be printed') does not specify who initiates printing or which component performs it, and omits what happens if printing is attempted when no entries exist.

findings.evidence: All data related to the word must be shown
findings.rationale: 'related to the word' and 'All data' are undefined—substring vs. exact-word matching, case sensitivity, searched fields, and whether full entry data (including passwords) is displayed are left open to interpretation.

findings.evidence: All data related to the word must be shown
findings.rationale: Describes the happy-path search output without specifying what happens when no entries match the input, which screen/action triggers the display, or which component renders it.

findings.evidence: A name is required in order for the new group/subgroup to be created
findings.rationale: States a required-name validation rule in passive voice without specifying the actor or what happens when a name is empty, missing, or invalid.

findings.evidence: A subgroup cannot be created when no group is selected
findings.rationale: Passive phrasing omits the actor and does not specify how the system handles an attempt to create a subgroup with no group selected (e.g., disabled control vs. error prompt).

findings.evidence: A name is required in order for the group/subgroup to be renamed
findings.rationale: States a required-name validation rule in passive voice without specifying the actor or how missing, empty, or invalid names are handled during renaming.

findings.evidence: find something in a group a word must be placed
findings.rationale: 'something' and 'a word' are vague—it is unclear what item types/fields are searched and whether multi-word queries or partial substrings are supported.

findings.evidence: a word must be placed in the find field
findings.rationale: Passive voice ('must be placed') omits the actor and system component executing the search, and omits behavior when the find field is empty or yields no matches.

findings.evidence: An entry must belong to a group to be created
findings.rationale: Clause attachment allows two readings: an entry can only be created inside an existing group, or a group requires an entry in order to be created.

findings.evidence: An entry must belong to a group to be created
findings.rationale: Passive phrasing omits the actor and does not specify what happens if entry creation is attempted when no group is selected or available.

findings.evidence: When the password field is completed the repeat password field must be completed
findings.rationale: Omits which screen/operation this applies to (entry vs. master password), the actor/validator, and the system behavior if the repeat password field is left blank.

findings.evidence: Password field and repeat password field must be identical
findings.rationale: States a password-matching validation rule without specifying which context it applies to or what error handling occurs when the two fields differ.

findings.evidence: An entry must be selected to be viewed or modified
findings.rationale: Passive voice omits the actor performing selection/viewing/modification and does not specify what happens if view or modify is invoked with no entry selected.

findings.evidence: When the password field is changed the repeat password field must be Changed and be identical with password field
findings.rationale: Passive phrasing omits the actor, applicable screen/context, and error behavior when the repeat password field is not updated or does not match.

findings.evidence: When the password field is changed the repeat password field must be Changed and be identical with password field
findings.rationale: Restates the repeat-password completion and equality rules already established in KP-012 and KP-013 without establishing a distinct scope or differing policy.

findings.evidence: An entry must be selected before it is duplicated
findings.rationale: Passive voice omits the actor and system component performing duplication and does not specify what happens if duplication is attempted without a selected entry.

findings.evidence: For the following features, use cases are not included
findings.rationale: 'the following features' has an unclear scope/reference across subsequent requirements, leaving unclear whether those features are out of scope or merely lack use-case documentation; 'a browser' is also unspecified.

findings.evidence: An internet connection and a browser are required in order to download new language translations For the following features, use cases are not included
findings.rationale: External dependencies (internet connection and browser) lack failure/offline error handling and actor ownership, and omitting use cases leaves behavioral details for following features incomplete.

findings.evidence: The prefix “Auto-Type:” is required in front of each sequence
findings.rationale: Does not specify where sequences are defined (e.g., an entry's note field) or what happens if the 'Auto-Type:' prefix is missing or malformed.

findings.evidence: Sequence’s length must not be more than a line (59 characters)
findings.rationale: Does not specify what happens when a sequence exceeds 59 characters (e.g., rejected, truncated, or ignored), nor whether the 59-character limit includes the 'Auto-Type:' prefix.

findings.evidence: If two auto-types are referred in one note field, only the first is used
findings.rationale: Passive voice omits the executing component, does not cover more than two auto-types in one note field, and omits whether extra auto-types are silently ignored or produce a warning/error.

findings.evidence: two auto-types
findings.rationale: Uses the term 'auto-types' instead of the term 'sequence' / 'Sequence' (with 'Auto-Type:' prefix) established in KP-018 and KP-019.

findings.evidence: Only one database file is allowed in command line options
findings.rationale: Placement of 'Only' creates ambiguity between allowing at most one database file alongside other options, requiring at least/exactly one database file, or disallowing any other command-line arguments.

findings.evidence: Only one database file is allowed in command line options
findings.rationale: Does not specify what happens if multiple database files are passed in command-line options (e.g., error and exit vs. opening only the first).

findings.evidence: In case a space is found in the path, it must be enclosed into quotes
findings.rationale: The pronoun 'it' has two plausible antecedents ('a space' vs. 'the path'), and the required quote type (single vs. double) is unspecified.

findings.evidence: In case a space is found in the path, it must be enclosed into quotes
findings.rationale: Passive voice omits who performs the quoting (user vs. system), which paths are subject to the rule, and what happens if a path containing spaces is not quoted.

findings.evidence: If a master password is required to unlock the database, the database doesn’t open unless the password is entered
findings.rationale: Specifies behavior when no password is entered but omits what happens when an incorrect master password is entered (e.g., error message, retry policy, lockout) and omits the actor.

findings.evidence: If a key file is required to unlock the database, the database doesn’t open unless the key file is present
findings.rationale: Omits what happens when the key file is missing, unreadable, corrupted, or incorrect (e.g., error message or browse prompt).

findings.evidence: If there is a composite key, both master password and key file are required
findings.rationale: Does not specify how a composite key is indicated/configured or what error handling occurs when only one credential is provided or either credential fails validation.

findings.evidence: File formats are not specialized password database formats
findings.rationale: 'specialized password database formats' is undefined and subjective, and 'File formats' does not clarify which formats are meant.

findings.evidence: File formats are not specialized password database formats
findings.rationale: Omits which file formats or operations (native '.kdb' storage vs. import/export formats) this constraint applies to.

findings.evidence: File formats only specify a low-level layout of stored data
findings.rationale: 'low-level layout' is vague and undefined, 'File formats' is unspecified, and the scope of 'only' is syntactically unclear.

findings.evidence: File formats only specify a low-level layout of stored data
findings.rationale: Does not identify which file formats are referenced or define/link the stored data layout specification.

findings.evidence: Global hot key cannot be changed
findings.rationale: Does not specify what the global hot key combination or triggered action is, nor what happens if a user tries to change it or if it conflicts with another shortcut.

findings.evidence: Title, username or URL cannot be changed in a TAN entry.
findings.rationale: States an immutability rule without specifying how attempts to modify those fields are handled (e.g., disabled UI fields vs. error message on save).

findings.evidence: When a TAN is used, it expires automatically and can never be used again.
findings.rationale: Passive phrasing omits what actions constitute 'used' (e.g., Auto-Type, copy, view), which component enforces expiration, and what happens if a user attempts to reuse an expired TAN.
